subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status be resolved from live gateway runtime health, a passive local plugin status contract, or the current `not checked` behavior?
rationale: Current main mitigates the old wording but does not implement the live-runtime health contract requested here, while the open fork PR and broader issue need an owner decision before another repair path is queued.

options.title: Make the broader live-gateway contract canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the remaining implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require external-memory live proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove `status --deep` plus JSON output against a real external memory plugin without local plugin side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as sufficient
options.body: Declare the current behavior good enough, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue with release evidence.

recommendation.title: Make the broader live-gateway contract canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 as the remaining implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require external-memory live proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent commits in the shared memory status surface and is a good owner for the remaining status contract choice.
